subject: computer-science
title: Hardware & Software: Storage
welcome_lead: Where do your files actually live? Inside spinning discs or flashing chips.
meta_desc: KS3 hardware: HDD, SSD, optical, units of storage.
final_note: More storage means more memories — and more responsibility.

concepts.def: Hard disk drive using spinning magnetic discs.
Solid-state drive using flash memory chips.
Storage read by laser, like a DVD.
Files saved on a server over the internet.
Extra copy kept in case the first is lost.
How much data a device can hold.

walkthroughs.body_html: An HDD uses spinning discs and a moving head — cheap, big, slower. An SSD has no moving parts — fast, quieter, more expensive per GB.
Cloud storage saves files on someone else's servers. Easy to share across devices but needs internet to access.
Three is the magic number: original, on-site backup, off-site backup. If a device fails, you still have your data.
